title: Read an upload, but never more than the limit

blocks.text: Reading a whole user-supplied file lets one huge upload exhaust memory. The page's fix **bounds the read itself**: read at most `limit + 1` bytes, and if more than `limit` arrived, refuse. A size checked beforehand (`Files.size`, `available()`) is not enough, because what is actually read can differ. Try-with-resources makes sure the stream is **closed on every path**.
Write `BoundedReader.read(in, limit)` that reads `in` as UTF-8 text:

items: up to `limit` bytes the text is returned;
more than `limit` bytes is refused with `SecurityException` (never a truncated text);
no more than `limit + 1` bytes are ever taken from `in`;
`in` is closed whether the read succeeds or not.

rows: 1000 bytes from a stream whose `available()` says 0

cases.says: A 12-byte UTF-8 upload read with a limit of 100 comes back as its text, and the stream is closed.
An upload of exactly the limit is read; one byte more is refused with SecurityException instead of being cut short.
A stream that reports 0 bytes available but holds 1000 bytes is refused at a limit of 10, and no more than 11 bytes are taken from it.
When the upload is too large, the stream is closed before SecurityException reaches the caller.

concepts: A user-supplied file is read with a bound on the bytes actually read (limit + 1), not after a size check that can go stale.
Try-with-resources closes streams on every path, preventing resource exhaustion.
